title: Activity and deployment reads expose bounded migration receipt facts
description: Producer child of task-78eedd8ebc2b43c581ac21ea28648a9a. Durable migration-receipt.ts22–36 has eleven members; APPLIED/REFUSED/REVERTED, applied[] meaning applied or undone files, nullable backupRef, failing basename in refusal.detail. COMMITTED is NOT APPLIED. Owner origin4253 adds existing /deployments/read via http/goal-deployment-read.ts and live-deployments.ts/live-goal-deployments.tsx; extend that after reconciliation, never create a duplicate endpoint/card. definitionOfDone: Real-store migration decisions project into existing activity and deployment/Runs read boundaries with explicit bounded environment, receipt identity, outcome, applied/reverted identifiers, nullable backup reference, and refusal code/layer/failing file. Reuse strict existing decoder; missing/corrupt/unverifiable evidence stays UNKNOWN/refused, not APPLIED or no pending work.

Receipt has no nodeRef/goalRef: expose and label project/environment observations as such, or require a real durable owner linkage from the producing decision. Never assign a receipt to a node/goal by matching filenames, SHA, latest timestamp, or arbitrary requestId. Goal-filtered reads must not bleed unrelated project evidence.

Pending versus applied is computed only from authoritative declared/bound migration identities and durable execution evidence from producer siblings; no browser directory scans or filename guesses. Missing declaration/source evidence is UNKNOWN, explicit empty is known-none. Tests include two migrations, two environments, APPLIED, REFUSED before backup, REFUSED after backup, REVERTED and corrupted receipt.

Backup is a non-download reference with hash only when verified as an existing confined backup; no database URL, password, SQL, full diagnostic output, credential hash/prefix or untrusted path reaches HTTP/logs/UI. Missing backup is not reported present; REFUSED may carry backupRef:null. Tests pin exact safe shape and code+layer.

Default production listener and browser exact decoders consume the new fields end to end; synchronize every exact-key/shape consumer. Existing auth/CSRF/read-only constraints hold; no new execution affordance. Fresh focused daemon/browser tests/typecheck and named broader gates have nonzero counts; parent78 remains presentation/live-journey consumer.
taskRails: Use existing activity/deployment read composition including owner-origin files after reconciliation; do not duplicate public surfaces.

THE BOUNDED PROJECTION — NEW `apps/daemon/src/deployment/migration-observation.ts` plus its one-line `.js` bridge, with a NAME-MATCHED `migration-observation.test.ts` in step 3. IT IS THE ONE PLACE a durable migration receipt becomes a safe, bounded, exposable fact, so both read boundaries share one decoder and one safety rule. INPUT: a project id and a DEPLOY RECEIPT already on the environment row. RESOLUTION IS A DURABLE KEY LOOKUP, NEVER A SEARCH: the deploy receipt's `decisionId` IS the migration `requestId`, so call `readMigrationReceipt(store, projectId, deployReceipt.decisionId)`. DO NOT enumerate `migration:` aggregates, and DO NOT select by filename, SHA, latest timestamp or arbitrary requestId — DoD 2 forbids exactly those. REUSE THE STRICT EXISTING DECODER: `readMigrationReceipt` already throws `MIGRATION_RECEIPT_INVALID` on a corrupt or unverifiable record; catch it and answer UNKNOWN-with-that-code, never APPLIED and never "no pending work". THREE DISTINCT ANSWERS, and the distinction is the point: NO receipt found (the deploy composed no migration — `ports.migrate` is optional, deploy-ports.ts:94) is UNKNOWN; a corrupt/unverifiable receipt is UNKNOWN carrying the decoder's code AND layer; a decoded receipt is a known observation. EXPOSE, all bounded: environment, receiptId, outcome (APPLIED | REFUSED | REVERTED), the applied/reverted identifiers, a nullable backup reference, and for a refusal its code, its layer and the FAILING FILE BASENAME ONLY. LABEL IT A PROJECT/ENVIRONMENT OBSERVATION — the receipt has no goalRef/nodeRef (eleven keys, migration-receipt.ts:22-36) and must never be presented as node or goal ownership (task rail 3). SAFETY IS ENFORCED HERE, ONCE: re-validate each applied entry with the existing `migrationFilename` guard rather than forwarding raw; bound the refusal detail to a basename; never emit a database URL, password, SQL, full diagnostic output, credential hash or prefix, or an untrusted path (DoD 4). The backup reference is a NON-DOWNLOAD reference with a hash only when verified as an existing confined backup; a missing backup reads missing, never present, and REFUSED may legitimately carry null. DO NOT change the eleven-key persisted receipt (task rail 2). Keep the module under 250 lines.

THE PROJECTION'S ARMS — NEW `apps/daemon/src/deployment/migration-observation.test.ts` (the name MUST match step 2's module exactly, or runtime-entrypoint.test.ts classes the module TEST tier and calls the bridge `unexpected`). THE MATRIX DoD 3 NAMES, ALL SIX: two migrations and two environments; APPLIED; REFUSED BEFORE BACKUP; REFUSED AFTER BACKUP; REVERTED; and a CORRUPTED receipt. Assert per case: the outcome, the applied/reverted identifiers BY VALUE AND BY COUNT (a projection that keeps only the first passes every single-identifier fixture), and the backup reference — present only where verified, null where the refusal preceded it. TWO ENVIRONMENTS DO NOT BLEED: a receipt for `staging` never appears on `production`'s observation and the reverse; assert the isolation directly rather than trusting the lookup. UNKNOWN VERSUS KNOWN-NONE, asserted as different answers: a deploy that composed no migration is UNKNOWN; a corrupt receipt is UNKNOWN carrying `MIGRATION_RECEIPT_INVALID` and its layer; neither may read as APPLIED or as "no pending work". Every refusal arm asserts the specific code AND the layer that answered, never merely that it refused (global rail 1). NO SECRET LEAKS, WITH A POSITIVE CONTROL: seed a credential-shaped value into the refusal detail and an untrusted path into the backup reference, assert the projection's output contains neither, and prove the assertion WOULD have caught them by checking it fires against the unbounded value. planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
ACTIVITY: ADD A MEMBER vs ADD A VERDICT KIND. Adding migration facts as new members of the activity entry was the obvious reading of "expose bounded migration receipt facts", and it is wrong here. The entry shape is exact-key at `live-activity.ts:91` and re-asserted as a literal roster in `plan-rejected-surfaces.test.tsx:191` and as full object fixtures in `board-screen.test.tsx` and `activity-screens.test.tsx`; growing it churns five files for a feed row that only needs to say WHAT HAPPENED. Adding the kind to `VERDICT_KINDS` renders the outcome word through the member that already exists, costs two files, and follows the DEPLOY_RECEIPT_COMMAND_KIND precedent in the same function. THE RICH BOUNDED FACTS GO ON THE DEPLOYMENT READ, which is where DoD 1's environment/receiptId/applied/backupRef/refusal actually belong and where a per-environment row already exists to carry them.

HOW THE RECEIPT IS FOUND: BY DURABLE KEY, NOT BY SEARCH. Enumerating `migration:` aggregates and picking per environment by latest `decidedAt` was considered and REJECTED - it is DoD 2's forbidden "latest timestamp" match and would attach an unrelated project receipt to an environment row. The deploy receipt's `decisionId` IS the migration `requestId` (finding 2), so the projection reads the deploy receipt already on the environment row and resolves its migration receipt by deterministic id. If that lookup finds nothing, the answer is UNKNOWN - never a fallback search.

WIRE-REQUIRED, TYPE-OPTIONAL for the new environment member. Making it required in the TS type breaks every type-literal builder (`needs-you-deploy.test.ts`, `needs-you-model.test.ts`, `live-environments.test.tsx`) for no behavioural gain. Making it optional in the type but REQUIRED in the browser exact-key roster keeps the blast radius to true wire frames while the decoder still fails closed on a frame that omits it. The risk of an optional type member is a producer that forgets to emit it; drill (iv) in step 7 exists precisely to prove the decoder refuses that frame rather than rendering nothing.

SPLIT CONSIDERED AND REJECTED. The row first measured at roughly twenty files, which is a split signal. But the epic is at 72 rows - well past the 40-row re-slice threshold where the rails say stop spinning out - and the over-scope dissolved once the Runs boundary (owned by task-de65294b) and the presentation layer (owned by task-78eedd8e per this row's own DoD 5) were excluded, and once the VERDICT_KINDS approach removed the activity fixture churn. What remains is one coherent row at eleven files. If the Runs boundary genuinely needs migration RECEIPT facts as well as declared identifiers, that is a comment and an amendment on task-de65294b, which already owns those two files - not a new row and not an eleventh and twelfth path here.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
MEASURED AT HEAD BY architect-d6d49adc 2026-09-07. Commands and results.

(1) THE SCOPE IS SMALLER THAN THE DoD TEXT READS, because two of the three named boundaries are owned by other rows. DoD 1 says "activity and deployment/Runs read boundaries". THE RUNS BOUNDARY IS NOT THIS ROW'S: task-122b55fd (WORKING, DoD 4) and its SPIDR child task-de65294b (PLANNING) own `/runs/read` and `live-runs.ts` for migration identifiers. Different facts (declared identifiers vs receipt observations), SAME TWO FILES - so editing them here is a shared-worktree collision, not a gap. DoD 5 also says "parent78 remains presentation/live-journey consumer", so `goal-deployments.tsx` and `live-goal-deployments.tsx` (the CARD) are task-78eedd8e's, not this row's. What is left, and what this plan takes: the ACTIVITY read boundary and the DEPLOYMENT read boundary plus their exact-key wire decoders.

(2) THE DURABLE JOIN EXISTS AND IS AUTHORITATIVE - this is the finding that makes DoD 2 satisfiable without guessing. `deploy-command.ts:267` passes `{ environment, requestId: decisionId, sha }`, so THE DEPLOY RECEIPT'S `decisionId` IS THE MIGRATION RECEIPT'S `requestId`. `deploy-receipt-contracts.ts:55` carries `decisionId`; `migrationReceiptId(projectId, requestId)` is deterministic; `readMigrationReceipt(store, projectId, requestId)` (migration-receipt.ts) resolves it directly. So the projection is a DURABLE KEY LOOKUP from a deploy receipt, never a filename, SHA, latest-timestamp or arbitrary-requestId match - exactly what DoD 2 forbids. No aggregate enumeration is needed.

(3) THE ACTIVITY BOUNDARY NEEDS NO SHAPE CHANGE, which removes about five files of fixture churn. `recordMigrationReceipt` commits with `commandKind: "internal.repository.migration_receipt"`, `principalId: "daemon:migration-engine"`, `targetAggregateId: "migration:<receiptId>"`, and the receipt's own `projectId`. In `activity-read.ts` `readActivity`, that decision ALREADY PASSES both filters today: `decision.key.projectId === projectId` holds, and `isSeatRecord` does not match (the kind is not in SEAT_KINDS, does not start with `session.`, and the target does not start with SEAT_TARGET_PREFIX). So migration decisions ALREADY APPEAR in project-scoped activity - with `verdict: null`, because the kind is absent from `VERDICT_KINDS` (:81-90). Adding the kind there plus an `outcome` branch in `verdictOf` - the DEPLOY_RECEIPT_COMMAND_KIND branch at :117-120 is the exact precedent - renders APPLIED/REFUSED/REVERTED as the EXISTING `verdict` member. The seven-member entry shape is UNCHANGED, so `live-activity.ts:91`'s exact-key roster, `plan-rejected-surfaces.test.tsx:191`, `board-screen.test.tsx:76-79` and `activity-screens.test.tsx:20-22` all stay untouched.

(4) GOAL SCOPING IS ALREADY HONEST BY CONSTRUCTION (DoD 2's "goal-filtered reads must not bleed"). Goal-scoped activity filters on a `targets` set built from the goal's aggregates; `migration:<receiptId>` is never in it, so a goal-filtered read excludes migration receipts today and must KEEP excluding them. The receipt genuinely has no goalRef/nodeRef (migration-receipt.ts:22-36, eleven keys: version, receiptId, requestId, projectId, environment, sha, decidedAt, applied, backupRef, outcome, refusal). This is a PROJECT/ENVIRONMENT observation and must be labelled as one.

(5) THE DEPLOYMENT READ SURFACE. `goal-deployment-read.ts` is 52 lines; `DeploymentEnvironmentRead` (:12-22) has NINE members and is built per environment over `ENVIRONMENT_NAMES` (:42). `live-deployments.ts:18` mirrors those nine EXACTLY in an `effectRecord` exact-key roster, and `:30` mirrors the five outer members. Exact-key means `Object.keys(value).length === names.length`, so any added wire member breaks every full literal frame.

(6) ASSERTING CONSUMERS, censused by SHAPE not symbol. FULL WIRE FRAMES that break on a roster change: `live-deployments.test.ts`, `cordum-app.test.tsx:980-983`, and `live-environments.test.tsx` (imports `mapDeploymentsAnswer` - step 1 confirms whether its frames are wire or type literals). TYPE-ONLY consumers, additive-safe, DO NOT TOUCH: `needs-you-deploy.ts` (reads only `row.target`/`row.environment`), `needs-you-model.ts`, `live-environments.tsx`, `live-goal-deployments.tsx`, `live-needs-you.tsx`.

(7) `ports.migrate` IS OPTIONAL (deploy-ports.ts:94, `readonly migrate?: DeployMigrationPort`) and `deploy-service.ts:156` returns null when absent. So a deploy whose composition did not ask for a migration produces NO migration receipt. That is DoD 1/3's UNKNOWN - genuinely distinct from a receipt that ran and applied nothing (known-none). The distinction is real in the data, not invented.

(8) DEPENDENCIES: task-2db55fca DONE (landed 2dfff1b2 - the producer whose receipts this row reads), task-c3291fe0 DONE, task-60008fcf WORKING, task-122b55fd WORKING. Two unmet, so the row is not claimable for WORKING until they land; dependsOn enforces it.
planningNotes.risks:
SECRET SURFACE IS THE HIGHEST RISK (epic rail 3, task rail 3, DoD 4). The receipt's `refusal.detail` is the engine's own text and is the one field that could carry more than a basename; `applied[]` entries are migration filenames guarded by `migrationFilename`; `backupRef` is a path. NOTHING from these may reach HTTP, a log or the UI unbounded: no database URL, password, SQL, full diagnostic output, credential hash or prefix, and no untrusted path. Bound and re-validate at the projection, do not forward raw, and give the leak arm a POSITIVE CONTROL or it passes vacuously.

BACKUP MUST NOT BE A DOWNLOAD AFFORDANCE (DoD 4, task rail 3). Expose a non-download reference with a hash only when verified as an existing confined backup. A missing backup is reported missing, never present. REFUSED legitimately carries `backupRef: null`.

OWNERSHIP MASQUERADE (DoD 2, task rail 3). The receipt has no goalRef/nodeRef. Everything this row exposes is a PROJECT/ENVIRONMENT observation and must be labelled as such. Goal-filtered activity must keep excluding `migration:<id>`; a change that makes it appear there would be a bleed, not a feature.

UNKNOWN IS NOT EMPTY (DoD 1, DoD 3, and the worker's own audit comment on this row). A historical receipt plus a current declaration does NOT establish current pending DB state. Missing declaration or missing execution evidence is UNKNOWN; only an explicit bound observation may read as known-none. Never compute pending by set-subtraction across receipt history, and never let a corrupt receipt read as APPLIED or as no-pending-work.

DO NOT EDIT `runs-read.ts` OR `live-runs.ts`. task-de65294b owns them and is unplanned; a concurrent edit collides in the shared worktree. If a step seems to need them, STOP and report rather than taking the path.

THE `.js` BRIDGE: a new daemon runtime module is unloadable by plain node without a physical bridge, and an unmatched test name makes `runtime-entrypoint.test.ts` class the module TEST tier and call the bridge `unexpected`. Name the test file to match the module exactly.
